questions.text: Which statement is a basic idea of cell theory?
options: All living things are made of one or more cells
Cells are only found in animals
All cells are the same size and shape
Living things are not made of cells
questions.explanation: Cell theory states that all living things are made of cells, and the cell is the basic unit of life.

questions.text: Which cell part controls what enters and leaves the cell?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane surrounds the cell and controls the movement of materials into and out of the cell.

questions.text: The human body has many systems working together. Which pair works most directly to deliver oxygen to your cells?
questions.explanation: The respiratory system takes in oxygen and the circulatory system carries it in the blood to cells throughout the body.

questions.text: Water has the chemical formula H2O. What does this formula tell you?
options: Each molecule has 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom
Water is made of only oxygen
questions.explanation: The formula H2O means each water molecule is made of two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.

questions.text: When a gas is cooled, its particles:
options: Slow down and move closer together
questions.explanation: Cooling removes energy, so particles slow down and move closer together. This can cause a gas to condense into a liquid.

questions.text: Two cars have the same mass. Car A moves faster than Car B. What is true about their kinetic energy?
options: Car A has more kinetic energy
Car B has more kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy increases with speed. With equal mass, the faster car (Car A) has more kinetic energy.

questions.text: Which design would best keep a hot drink warm the longest?
options: An insulated cup with a lid
A thin plastic cup with no lid
questions.explanation: Insulation slows the transfer of thermal energy. An insulated cup with a lid keeps heat from escaping, so the drink stays warm.

questions.text: In the water cycle, what process turns liquid water into water vapor in the air?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is when liquid water gains energy from the Sun and changes into water vapor, a gas, in the atmosphere.

questions.text: Clouds form when water vapor rises, cools, and:
options: Sinks to the ground as a solid
questions.explanation: As water vapor rises and cools, it condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds. This is part of the water cycle.

questions.text: A weather map shows a cold air mass moving toward a warm air mass. This boundary, called a front, often brings:
questions.explanation: When air masses of different temperatures meet at a front, the rising warm air often forms clouds and storms.

questions.text: Areas near the equator are generally warmer than areas near the poles mainly because:
options: Sunlight strikes the equator more directly
The equator is closer to the Sun by millions of miles
The poles have no Sun ever
The equator is made of hotter rock
questions.explanation: Near the equator, sunlight hits Earth more directly and concentrates energy, making it warmer than the poles, where light is more spread out.

questions.text: During photosynthesis, plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make:
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar (food) for the plant and releases oxygen.

questions.text: In an ecosystem, a sudden drop in the number of plants would most directly affect:
questions.explanation: Organisms depend on resources. Fewer plants means less food for plant-eaters (herbivores), so their population is affected first.

questions.text: Coal, oil, and natural gas are called fossil fuels. They are considered nonrenewable because:
options: They take millions of years to form
They can be made in a day
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels form from ancient organisms over millions of years, so they cannot be replaced quickly and are nonrenewable.

questions.text: A student mixes two clear liquids and a solid forms at the bottom. This is the BEST evidence that:
options: A chemical reaction produced a new substance
questions.explanation: Forming a solid (precipitate) from two liquids is a sign of a chemical reaction, where new substances with new properties form.

questions.text: Before designing a solution, engineers define the criteria and constraints. A constraint is best described as:
options: A limit the design must work within, such as cost or size
A goal the design should achieve
questions.explanation: Constraints are the limits on a design, such as budget, materials, time, or size. Criteria are the goals the design must meet.

questions.text: Which action would most reduce human impact on a local river's water quality?
options: Reducing fertilizer and waste runoff into the river
Adding more trash to the river
Removing all plants along the banks
questions.explanation: Runoff of fertilizer and waste pollutes rivers. Reducing that runoff lowers human impact and protects water quality.

questions.text: You touch a hot stove and pull your hand away instantly. Which system sensed the heat and sent the signal?
questions.explanation: The nervous system uses sensory receptors to detect stimuli like heat and sends signals that trigger a fast response.
